- **AgentClient:** It's a vanilla JavaScript/TypeScript class for any environment. It provides RPC calls, state sync, streaming, and auto-reconnection, and it sits alongside the React `useAgent` hook and the HTTP-only `agentFetch` client (The table lists useAgent, AgentClient, and agentFetch, with AgentClient described as a vanilla JavaScript/TypeScript class for any environment.).
- **Typed RPC:** A changelog entry says AgentClient can take an agent type parameter for typed calls and exposes a stub proxy for RPC-style method calls (AgentClient accepts an optional agent type parameter, which gives full type inference on RPC calls.). The RPC type utilities are exported from `agents/client` (AgentMethods, AgentStub, and RPCMethods are exported from agents/client.).
- **Decorator scope:** The `@callable()` decorator is needed only for calls from external runtimes such as browsers or other services. Calls from within the same Worker can use Durable Object RPC on the stub directly (@callable() is only required for methods called from external runtimes, and same-Worker calls can use standard Durable Object RPC without the decorator.).
- **Agent-to-MCP RPC:** Agents SDK v0.6.0 lets an Agent and an McpAgent in the same Worker connect over RPC instead of HTTP (The release lets you define an Agent and an McpAgent in the same Worker and connect them over RPC.).

content.content:
No, this page doesn't mention Cap'n Web or capnweb.

**How AgentClient handles RPC:**

- **`agent.call(method, args?, options?)`** invokes a method on the agent by name. Arguments go in an array, and the call returns a Promise with the result. For example, `client.call("sendMessage", ["Hello!"])`.
- **`agent.stub`** offers a proxy syntax for the same calls, so you pass arguments directly instead of wrapping them in an array. The page shows it on the `useAgent` object, and its reference table for `AgentClient` doesn't list it. Passing your Agent class as a type parameter makes stub methods fully typed.
- **Methods must be exposed with `@callable()`** when called from external runtimes like browsers. Calls made within the same Worker can use standard Durable Object RPC on the stub without the decorator.
- **Streaming** is enabled by marking a method as streaming on the agent side. On the client, the `call` options accept `onChunk`, `onDone`, and `onError` callbacks.

The search turned up the Cloudflare Agents SDK changes that add a Cap'n Web transport to `AgentClient`.

- **Release 0.24.0:** It added a Cap'n Web transport for plain Durable Objects that use WebSockets, which the release notes describe as WebSockets speaks the Agent protocol for plain hosts, and gains a Cap'n Web transport.
- **Choosing the wire:** Both `useAgent` and `AgentClient` take a transport option. The default is the hibernating WebSocket, while the `capnweb` option opens a single Cap'n Web session that carries protocol frames and serves methods directly (useAgent({ transport }) and AgentClient({ transport }) pick the wire. "cf-websocket" (default) is the hibernating socket; call()/stub send JSON rpc frames. "capnweb" runs one Cap'n Web session that carries protocol frames and serves callables natively).
- **Behaviour on capnweb:** Per the 0.24.0 notes, the Durable Object stays in memory while a Cap'n Web connection is open (index 1-11).
- **Removed endpoint:** The experimental `?__agents_rpc=capnweb` endpoint from 0.23.0 was removed (index 1-13).
- **Regular Agents:** According to the lifecycle docs, `@callable()` methods on a regular Agent are not exposed on the Cap'n Web root. An Agent that wants native calls has to pass a callables target instead (index 2-10).
- **Source:** The changes come from pull request #2249 by mattzcarey, which replaced the earlier #2156 (index 3-2).

The search did not surface any `AgentClient` code examples for the Cap'n Web transport, so the details above come from release notes, docs, and the PR description rather than a usage guide. A separate result, a ProSkills issue, points to a `capnweb` skill in the cloudflare/computer repo, but it is only a candidate listing and doesn't describe the agents API.

content.text:
In `agents` 0.24.0 or later, pass `transport: "capnweb"` when you create the client, e.g. `new AgentClient({ ..., transport: "capnweb" })` (`useAgent` takes the same option). The default is `"cf-websocket"`, the hibernating WebSocket that sends `call()`/`stub` as JSON `rpc` frames. With `"capnweb"`, a single Cap'n Web session carries everything, and `client.call(...)` or `client.stub.method(...)` call server methods directly: a returned `RpcTarget` arrives as a live stub, a `ReadableStream` streams, and calls can be pipelined.

On the server, `@callable()` methods are not exposed over Cap'n Web, because they stay the JSON-wire interface. An Agent that wants native Cap'n Web calls has to pass a `callables` option: an `RpcTarget` whose prototype methods become the remote interface.

Two trade-offs: the Durable Object stays in memory while a Cap'n Web connection is open, so it doesn't hibernate, and PartySocket still handles reconnection. The experimental `?__agents_rpc=capnweb` endpoint from 0.23.0 has been removed. The release notes include no full code example, so check PR #2249 for exact `callables` usage.

Sources:
- [agents@0.24.0 release notes](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/releases/tag/agents%400.24.0)
- [PR #2249: Cap'n Web transport](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/pull/2249)
- [Agents lifecycle docs](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/main/docs/agents/lifecycle.md)
- [Client SDK docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/api-reference/client-sdk)
